Subject: DPA evidence: inventory & mapping request

Hi Hannah,

We're working through our DPA annex and need an evidence package from Redwood to close out a privacy review. Can you provide the following within 5 business days if possible?

- Full list of subprocessors (names, country, purpose) and the last attestation date
- Data classification mapping (which fields you consider PII/sensitive for API telemetry, embeddings, and stored artifacts)
- KMS/custody model and which keys are customer-controlled vs Redwood-managed
- Sample dataflow diagram (showing telemetry, KV cache, model hosting, and any export paths)
- Any proof points for pseudonymization/minimization applied during inference (if applicable)

We can accept a zipped evidence pack or a shared Drive folder. If there are items that require an NDA or additional paperwork, call that out.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if useful.

Anika Rao
Head of Privacy, Medicore
anika.rao@medicore.com

Hi Anika — looping in technical artifacts.

Attached is a sanitized subprocessor summary (subprocessors-202611.pdf) that includes locations and the minimal purpose statements. Highlights:

- Most subprocessors are for infra (GCP/Azure regions), observability, and managed model hosting.
- For any managed hosting partner that handles decrypted material at rest we include controls and SOC2 references.

Data classification (high level):
- Inputs: may contain PII (customer-controlled); by default Hosted API treats inputs as transient unless retention is enabled.
- Outputs: model generations can be considered derived data; customers control retention and forwarding rules.
- Telemetry: aggregated token-level telemetry used for performance/quality is pseudonymized; request-level metadata (request ID, timestamp) is retained for X days depending on region and plan.

Operational note: for regulated PII where customers require strict custody, we recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed keys. We'll call out which subprocessors are used per deployment mode in the folder.

Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the diagram and retention questions?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Dataflow diagram + role justifications

Hi Anika — attaching the editable diagram and pasting a concise dataflow plus role justification inline. See drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleDataflow (editable folder).

Simple ASCII dataflow (first-pass):
Client App --> [Edge Router (regional)] --> [Redwood Inference API (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)]
  - API forwards request to Serving Runtime -> Model Replica (GPU)
  - KV cache (regional) holds prefix cache (TTL configurable)
  - Telemetry collector (pseudonymizes IDs) -> Aggregation store (retention policy)
  - If retention enabled: Storage (S3) encrypted under KMS key (customer-managed for Private)
  - Subprocessors: infra provider, metrics vendor, observability; see subprocessors manifest for mapping

Role justifications (short):
- Platform Ops: incident response and infra provisioning; access limited to transient logs and aggregated telemetry; no access to customer-managed keys.
- Model Ops: deploys / rolls model binaries; does not have access to raw customer inputs if customer keys are used.
- Security Team: audit log access for compliance; access is gated via ticketing and reviewed quarterly.

Pseudonymization example (narrative):
- We hash user identifiers with a salt unique per-tenant before aggregation; raw identifiers are not stored in the aggregation store. Traces retaining request ids keep only an opaque request token; mapping back to an identifier requires an internal ticketed process and is logged.

Attachment(s): dataflow-pcii-20261202.vsdx

Let us know if you need explicit export-country mapping and we'll add a column to the manifest.

—Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA evidence: inventory & mapping request — package summary

Anika — summary and next steps. Thanks for the pointed questions; attached is the preliminary evidence folder and a checklist for Medicore's DPA review. Deliverable notes below and immediate answers to your two bullets.

Immediate answers (in-thread):
1) Telemetry pseudonymization sample: we perform tenant-scoped HMAC with a rotating salt (rotated monthly) over any identifier before aggregation. HMAC seeds are stored in an HSM; only the Security team can request unmasking via a ticket. We'll include a short pseudonymization narrative file in the folder.
2) Export / cross-border exposures: Hosted: depending on nearest region the request may be routed through infra in other regions for failover; we list all possible egress countries per subprocessor in the manifest. Dedicated: generally constrained to the region assigned but some telemetry copies to observability vendors may be cross-region; Private: customer-managed keys and networking keep data in your VPC by default. We'll add an explicit 'egress_countries' column to the CSV.

Deliverable (attached to shared Drive):
- redwood-evidence-pack/
  - subprocessors-202611.pdf
  - redwood-dpa-subprocessor-inventory.csv (with egress_countries column)
  - dataflow-pcii-20261202.vsdx (editable)
  - pseudonymization-narrative.txt
  - kms-custody-table.csv
  - soc2-type2-2026.pdf (pointer / redacted excerpt)

We aim to have the explicit egress_country mapping and the signed DPA exhibit (if you need it) by EOD 2026-12-06. If Medicore prefers a walkthrough, propose 2026-12-04 10:00–10:30 PST — I can host and Marissa and Jordan will attend.

Thanks — we'll keep this thread as the canonical evidence log.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): (see Drive folder)
